issues.title: The sizing bound is not the largest in-flight count one stack can reach: the window bounds a loop, not a stack, and straight-line groups and nesting exceed it

rounds.argument:
Section 5 (PARK-ON-MISS.md:718-724) sizes completion records as 'at least the per-stack in-flight window times the stack count: one stack cannot have more operations outstanding than the window the emitter fixes, which is WF_BRIDGE_OPERATION_CAPACITY / 2 today (bridge.c:857)'. That number does not bound a stack. wf__completion_window is the staged-pipeline query, asked once per loop entry and never per iteration (bridge.h:30-35); its own body clamps by ring capacity, helper count, the compiler ceiling, the loop span and the slot-byte budget (bridge.c:845-887). It bounds one loop's in-flight iterations, not one stack's outstanding operations.

Two lowerings the emitter has today exceed it. A straight-line [PAR-1] window with N may-suspend members holds N records at once: emit_overlap_joins dispatches completion members in place and joins them at the group's join site (parallel.rs:631-637), so every member submitted before that site is outstanding, and N is a source-fixed statement count that never reaches wf__completion_window. The tree already generates exactly this shape at an arbitrary N: more_than_target_capacity_reads(count) (tests/completion.rs:438-457) emits count straight-line read_at calls in one region, and its name says what it is for. And nesting sums them: section 0's second shape is a may-suspend call reached through recursion or a compute hand-out, and S23 walks a stack holding two waiting frames, so a stack's outstanding count is the sum over its live frames, bounded only by recursion depth, which the ledger bounds in bytes and not in operations.

So records >= window x stacks is not sufficient, and no emitter-fixed number makes it sufficient as the plan states it. This is load-bearing rather than a wording point: decision 55 deletes every refusal path on the strength of this bound, so a claim that fails now has no arm to take at all, which is worse than the refusal that was removed. Either the bound is stated over what actually holds records — the per-frame outstanding count summed over a stack's live frames — and something caps it, or the emitter caps outstanding operations per stack and the plan says where. Section 11 item 22 (:2081-2086) is well built and would catch this: with records at the stated bound and a straight-line group of N > window, its refusal assertion fails.

issues.title: Section 8's deletion list says six _direct symbols where the cited dispatch names five, leaving directory-next's direct route unnamed

rounds.argument:
Section 8 (PARK-ON-MISS.md:1505-1507) deletes 'the dispatch that names the six _direct symbols (compiler/src/backend/qualification.rs:233-291)'. That range names five: close at :235-236, open_at at :246-247, status at :257-258, pread at :276-277, write at :286-287. A sixth direct symbol exists — wf__completion_directory_next_direct, defined at windows_runtime.c:1617 — and it is not in the cited range; qualification.rs:1036 also names a _direct symbol (native_file_status_symbol) outside it. The count came in with decision 46 and was carried forward.

Under the earlier drafts this was arithmetic. Under decision 55 the completeness of this list is the ruling's substance: the direct family leaves emitted code, so a direct route the deletion list does not name is a per-operation blocking call the ruling forbids and the plan does not delete. Either directory_next reaches its direct symbol by another route that section 8 should name, or it has no direct route and the count is five.
